name: Annual budget and guidance (single-mine gold producer)
summary: Each autumn the company turns the mine's annual production plan into an operating, capital and exploration budget for the next year, gets it approved by the board in December and publishes production, cost and capital guidance in mid-January. Mine, mill and maintenance superintendents build department budgets in spreadsheets, the site controller and GM consolidate and negotiate them, and head office adds exploration, corporate costs, tax and gold price scenarios. It is slow because superintendents work on rotation and fit the budget around production, because the budget goes back and forth several times between site and head office, and because the board meeting and the January release are fixed dates.

baseline.org_archetype: A TSX-listed single-mine gold producer with one underground mine and mill in northern Ontario, an exploration property in Quebec and a small Toronto head office, budgeting in spreadsheets.
baseline.notes: Clock starts when technical services delivers the annual production plan (about early October) and stops when guidance is published in mid-January. In 2020 and 2021 most site reviews were by video.

unit_of_work: one annual budget and its public guidance
trigger: Technical services delivers the life-of-mine and annual production plan for the next year.
end_state: The board has approved the budget, it is loaded in the ERP and issued to the site and exploration, and guidance is published by news release.

volume.seasonality: One cycle a year, October to mid-January. A lighter mid-year reforecast is not modelled here.

evidence.note: One budget and one guidance release a year (January 14, 2021 for 2021); 1/12 = 0.083 a month.
Sets assumptions, runs scenarios and takes the budget through executive and board review; about 60-80 hours a year.
Leads the site budget challenge, including a site visit; about 40-60 hours a year.
Executive review and guidance release approval.
Owns the budget templates, the consolidated corporate model and the board package; about 120-150 hours a year.
Tax, mining tax, royalty and cash flow schedules for the budget model.
Reviews the site budget with the superintendents and defends it to the COO.
Loads the production plan, coordinates departments and consolidates the site budget, with help from site accountants; about 120-150 hours a year.
Builds the underground mining budget: labour, consumables per metre, contractors, equipment hours and capital development.
Builds the processing and assay laboratory budget.
Builds the maintenance budget and the sustaining capital equipment list.
Prices the exploration program for the mine and the Quebec property.
Headcount plan, wage escalation and benefits loading.

roles.title: Vice-president, investor relations and corporate development

evidence.note: Drafts the guidance news release.
Reviews the guidance release for forward-looking information requirements.

systems.name: Mid-market ERP for finance, purchasing, inventory and fixed assets
Mine design and scheduling software (3D design, scheduling)
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Newswire distribution service (guidance news release dissemination)

resources.name: Camps (100-person camp at the mine and a smaller camp at the mill)

steps.name: Set budget calendar and price assumptions
steps.description: Once technical services delivers the annual production plan, the CFO issues the budget memo: timetable to the December board meeting, gold price and US dollar exchange rate deck (usually a discount to consensus), diesel and power prices and wage escalation. The memo goes to the GM, the corporate controller and the vice-president of exploration.

error.defect_description: A price or FX assumption out of line with peers, challenged later by the board.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian gold producers; the timetable is set back from a December board approval and January guidance.

steps.name: Issue budget templates
steps.description: The corporate controller rolls forward last year's budget workbooks by department and cost centre, updates the assumption tab from the CFO's deck and links the production physicals (tonnes, grade, ounces, development metres) that each department budget must use.

error.defect_description: A broken link or last year's rate left in a template.

evidence.note: Spreadsheet budgeting is the norm at a single-mine producer without planning software.

steps.name: Load production plan and launch site budget
steps.description: The site controller loads the monthly production plan from the mine planning output into the templates, adds the current headcount roster and runs a kickoff meeting with the superintendents to explain the deadline, the cost-per-tonne target and what has changed since last year.

error.defect_description: Physicals keyed for the wrong month or an old version of the plan.

evidence.note: Author's description of common site practice.

steps.name: Build underground mining budget
steps.description: The mine superintendent, with the mine captains and a mine engineer, prices each crew and heading: labour by rotation crew, explosives, bolts and drill steel per metre, diamond drilling and raise contractors, equipment operating hours and capitalised development. He works on it during his 14-day rotation on site alongside his normal duties.

error.defect_description: Unit rates or crew counts inconsistent with the plan, or contractor work double counted with the capital list.

evidence.note: Superintendents on a 14/14 rotation can only work on the budget while on site; the 1-3 week wait reflects rotation timing and production priorities.

steps.name: Build processing and laboratory budget
steps.description: The mill superintendent prices reagents per tonne milled (cyanide, lime, carbon), grinding media, power, mill and laboratory labour, assay consumables and the planned shutdowns, using the throughput and grade in the plan.

error.defect_description: Reagent consumption rate from an outdated period.

evidence.note: Built in parallel with the mine budget.

steps.name: Build maintenance budget and sustaining capital list
steps.description: The maintenance superintendent builds labour, parts and contractor costs from the component rebuild schedule and fleet hours, and lists sustaining capital items such as replacement scooptrams, haul trucks and pumps with quotes or last prices.

error.defect_description: Equipment replacement listed both as capital and as a maintenance rebuild.

evidence.note: Built in parallel with the mine and mill budgets.

steps.name: Price exploration program
steps.description: The vice-president of exploration turns the proposed exploration program into a budget: metres by target and drilling type at the mine and on the Quebec property, contractor rates, assays, geologists and the care-and-maintenance cost of the Quebec site.

error.defect_description: Drill metres priced at last year's contractor rate.

evidence.note: Wesdome's 2021 guidance gives exploration dollars and metres by mine and drilling type, so the budget is built at that level; hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare headcount and wage plan
steps.description: The HR director sets the headcount plan by department, wage escalation, benefits loading and rotation travel cost per head, and sends it to the site controller and the corporate controller.

error.defect_description: Vacancies budgeted at full year instead of from expected hire date.

evidence.note: Common practice; runs alongside the department budgets.

steps.name: Consolidate site budget
steps.description: The site controller, helped by a site accountant, collects the last department workbooks, pulls them into the site budget, removes double counts and compares cost per tonne, cost per ounce and capital with the current-year forecast. Departments that are late are chased by email and radio.

error.defect_description: A department version overwritten by an older file.

evidence.note: Waiting for the slowest department submission; consolidation in spreadsheets.

steps.name: GM reviews site budget
steps.description: The general manager goes through the site budget with each superintendent, pushes cost per tonne towards the target and decides which capital items go forward. Departments whose budgets do not fit are sent back to rework them.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: GM accountable for the site budget

evidence.note: APQC reports a median of five budget versions, mostly from back-and-forth negotiation; the 20% rework loop here is one of those rounds. Review hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: COO travels to site
steps.description: The COO flies from Toronto to Sault Ste. Marie and drives about three hours to the mine, stays overnight in the camp and returns after the review. In 2020 and 2021 travel restrictions pushed most of these reviews to video.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

evidence.note: Route and drive time are the author's estimate for a mine near Wawa; touch covers both directions. Weather can cancel the regional flight, which shows up as a longer wait.

steps.name: Challenge site budget with the COO
steps.description: The COO, with the GM, site controller and superintendents, walks through each department, development metres, mill throughput and the capital list, compares cost per tonne with peers and the prior year, and sets cuts or additions.

error.defect_description: A cut agreed in the meeting is not carried into the workbook.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: COO approval of the site operating and capital budget

evidence.note: Common practice at producers where the COO is accountable for site costs; another negotiation round.

steps.name: Build consolidated corporate model
steps.description: The corporate controller loads the site budget, the exploration budget, corporate G&A and the Quebec care-and-maintenance costs into the corporate model and calculates ounces sold, cash cost and all-in sustaining cost per ounce, capital, cash flow and the year-end cash balance by month.

error.defect_description: Sustaining and growth capital split inconsistent with the reporting definition.

evidence.note: Guidance items published by Wesdome (production, cash cost, AISC, sustaining and growth capital, exploration, G&A) define the outputs the model must produce; AISC follows the WGC guidance note.

steps.name: Add tax, royalty and cash flow schedules
steps.description: The treasury and tax manager adds income tax, Ontario mining tax and royalty schedules, the timing of tax instalments and any financing costs, and checks the year-end cash balance against the treasury minimum.

error.defect_description: Mining tax calculated on the wrong base.

evidence.note: Runs alongside the corporate model build.

steps.name: Run price and cost scenarios
steps.description: The CFO runs sensitivities on gold price, exchange rate, head grade and mill throughput, checks liquidity under the low case and proposes the production, cost and capital ranges to be published as guidance.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

evidence.note: Guidance is published as ranges for production, grade, unit costs and capital; scenario method and hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Executive review of budget and guidance
steps.description: The CEO meets the CFO, COO and vice-president of exploration to settle guidance ranges, capital priorities and the size of the exploration program. They either accept the model or send it back for site cuts or corporate changes.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

evidence.note: APQC reports a median of five versions; the two loops here are further negotiation rounds. Probabilities are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft board budget package
steps.description: The corporate controller writes the board budget book and slides: production and cost summary, capital list, exploration program, headcount, scenarios, risks and the proposed guidance, with reconciliation to the current-year forecast.

error.defect_description: A slide number differs from the model after a late change.

evidence.note: Common board budget package content.

steps.name: Sign off and circulate package to the board
steps.description: The CFO reviews the package with the CEO, makes final edits and sends it to the directors through the board secretary about a week before the meeting.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

evidence.note: Common governance practice.

steps.name: Board reviews and approves budget
steps.description: At its scheduled December meeting the board questions the price assumptions, unit costs, capital and exploration spending and approves the budget and guidance, or asks for changes to be brought back at a follow-up call.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

control.basis: Board mandate: approval of the annual operating and capital budget

evidence.note: December approval as stated in the organisation file; the wait is the slack between a ready package and the fixed meeting date.

steps.name: Load approved budget and issue plans
steps.description: The site controller loads the monthly budget by cost centre into the ERP for variance reporting, and the approved budget goes to technical services for the short-range plan, to HR as the headcount plan and to exploration as the approved program.

error.defect_description: Budget phased evenly by month instead of following the production plan.

evidence.note: Load happens before January so variance reporting starts with the new year; holidays add to the wait.

steps.name: Draft guidance news release
steps.description: After the year-end production numbers are in, the vice-president of investor relations drafts the release that combines fourth-quarter and annual production with next year's guidance by mine: production, head grade, unit costs, capital, exploration metres and dollars, and corporate G&A.

error.defect_description: A guidance range typed differently from the board-approved figure.

evidence.note: Wesdome released its 2021 guidance with 2020 fourth-quarter production on January 14, 2021; the wait from board approval is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Legal and disclosure committee review
steps.description: The general counsel checks that the guidance is labelled as forward-looking, that the material assumptions (gold price, exchange rate, grades) and risk factors are stated and that production figures agree with the qualified person's numbers, and the disclosure committee approves the wording.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

evidence.note: NI 51-102 Part 4A requires a reasonable basis, cautionary language and the material assumptions for forward-looking information.

steps.name: Approve and issue guidance release
steps.description: The CEO approves the final release, which goes out on the newswire after market close and is filed on SEDAR and posted on the website.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

control.basis: Disclosure policy: CEO approval of material news releases

evidence.note: Guidance published by news release; approval step is common practice.

exceptions.name: Departments rework after GM review
exceptions.description: The GM finds cost per tonne above target or capital too high and sends department budgets back.

exceptions.name: Site revision after COO challenge
exceptions.description: The COO's review sets cuts that the site has to work back into the budget.

exceptions.name: Executive sends budget back
exceptions.description: The executive review asks for site cuts or corporate model changes before the board package.

exceptions.name: Board asks for changes
exceptions.description: The board asks for a revised price deck or capital list and approves at a follow-up call.

exceptions.name: Site visit cancelled
exceptions.description: Travel restrictions or weather on the regional flight move the COO review to video.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from annual production plan to published guidance
benchmarks.population: Single-mine Canadian gold producer; guidance published January 14, 2021

evidence.note: The end date is Wesdome's January 14, 2021 guidance release; the early-October start is the author's estimate, so the cycle length is tier C. p90 allows for a late production plan or a board follow-up call.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from budget objectives to ready-to-use budget (25th percentile or better)
benchmarks.population: APQC Open Standards Benchmarking, more than 3,900 organisations, cross-industry

evidence.note: Top performers 25 days or less, about half the 75th percentile. The comparable span in this file, s01 to s17, simulates at a median of about 53 days, close to the 75th percentile implied by the article (about twice 25 days).
Median organisation produces five versions of the budget.

pain_points.description: Superintendents on a 14/14 rotation build their budgets around production and can only work on them while on site, so department submissions arrive late and unevenly.

evidence.note: Rotation schedules from the organisation file; effect on budget timing is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Several rounds of negotiation between departments, the GM, the COO and the executive team each re-open the spreadsheets, with version control by file name.

evidence.note: APQC: a median of five versions and most cycle time spent waiting for inputs and responses.

pain_points.description: Sustaining versus growth capital classification decides the published AISC guidance and is argued late in the cycle.

evidence.note: Guidance publishes AISC and separate sustaining and growth capital ranges; classification is left to management under the WGC guidance.

pain_points.description: The December board date and the January release are fixed, so slippage in the site build compresses the head-office model and scenario work rather than moving the dates.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice.

assumptions: The cycle runs from delivery of the annual production plan by technical services (about early October) to the guidance release (mid-January). The production plan itself belongs to ts-lom-planning.
Exploration planning (expl-planning) supplies the program; this file covers only pricing it for the budget (s07).
Loaded costs are taken from the organisation file. The COO site visit uses one camp room for one or two nights; flights and drive are counted as travel time in touch_min.

Probabilities for the rework loops (GM 20%, COO 20%, executive 25%, board 10%) are the author's estimate. Each review round (GM, COO, executive, board) already produces a revised version, so a budget with no loops has four or five versions and one with loops six or more, close to the APQC median of five.
The board is an external party; its meeting carries no labour cost here and the wait before it is slack until the scheduled December date.
Roles state about 0.37 FTE in total; the implied FTE from hands-on time is lower because the stated figures include preparation and meeting time outside the itemised steps.

The organisation file lists only cfo, coo, ceo, corp-controller and gm for this process; this file adds site-controller, mine-superintendent, mill-superintendent, maint-superintendent, vp-exploration, hr-director, treasury-tax-manager, vp-ir and general-counsel, all present in the organisation file.
cases_per_month is 0.083 (one a year), not the organisation file's 0.1 mode and 0.17 high, which would imply a second full budget each year.
The organisation file's produces list has no public guidance output; this file adds news_release to shareholders and osc-tsx.

The simulated median of about 94 days is close to the 100-day benchmark, but the simulated p90 of about 130 days exceeds the 115-day estimate. In practice the December board date and the mid-January release are fixed, so extra negotiation rounds squeeze review time instead of pushing the dates; the simulation cannot pin dates, so its tail is longer than reality.

Organisation file corrected on 2026-11-24 to match this workflow's sources: ids were renamed (mill-elution-refining to mill-gold-room-refining, loaded_carbon to gold_concentrate, tailings_slurry to filtered_tailings, elution-circuit to refinery), and roles and resources this workflow added are now in the organisation file. Notes above that describe a mismatch refer to the file before the correction.

sources.title: Wesdome Announces 2020 Fourth Quarter and Full Year Production Results; Provides 2021 Guidance
sources.publisher: Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd. (news release, via Yahoo Finance)
sources.supports: Released January 14, 2021 with fourth-quarter production: 2021 guidance for production by mine, head grade, cash operating cost and AISC per ounce, sustaining and growth capital by mine, exploration budget (C$32M) and metres by mine and drilling type, and corporate G&A (C$8-9M); Kiena figures contingent on a restart decision.

sources.title: Cycle Time to Complete the Annual Budget: Metric of the Month
sources.supports: APQC data from more than 3,900 organisations: top performers complete the annual budget in 25 calendar days or less, about half the time of the 75th percentile; the measure runs from setting budget objectives to a ready-to-use budget; the median organisation produces five versions of the budget; much of the cycle time is waiting for inputs or responses and back-and-forth negotiation.

sources.title: World Gold Council publishes update to its Guidance Note on Non-GAAP Metrics
sources.supports: Updated guidance on all-in sustaining cost and all-in cost published 14 November 2018, first issued June 2013, usable from 1 January 2019; companies are responsible for their own reporting and all gold miners are encouraged to use the metrics.

sources.title: National Instrument 51-102 Continuous Disclosure Obligations (consolidated text)
sources.publisher: British Columbia Securities Commission (Canadian Securities Administrators instrument)
sources.supports: s.4.1(2) annual statements must be audited; s.4.2 non-venture issuers file audited annual statements within 90 days of year end; s.4.3(3) interim statements not reviewed by an auditor must carry a notice saying so; s.4.4 interim statements within 45 days of period end; s.4.5 board approves annual and interim statements before filing and may delegate interim approval to the audit committee; s.5.5 the same for MD&A; s.6.2 AIF within 90 days; Part 4A forward-looking information needs a reasonable basis, cautionary language and the material assumptions; Part 4B FOFI and financial outlooks. The consolidation opened shows no version date; it uses pre-IFRS wording ('interim financial statements') and already contains Parts 4A and 4B. The 45-day and 90-day deadlines and the approval rules were unchanged in 2019-2022.
